dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Hmph. Young people nowadays have no work ethic worth mentioning!

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: They slack off at key times and care so much about the holidays, yet know nothing of enterprise or responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: If everyone was this lax in their duties, we wouldn't have managed to construct a single small fishing boat, let alone the Jade Chamber!

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Hmph. The younger generation are nothing but slackers these days.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You are...?

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: I'm the Dockyard Manager here in Liyue Harbor. Name's Xiao. Is there something I can help you with? If not, I need to get back to work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, about your work...

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Work? Bah! Don't get me started! Young people these days... No expertise, zero sense of responsibility, they don't bother to tell you when they aren't going to show up, and when they do show up... Half the time they do more harm than good, and the other half they expect you to applaud every word that comes out of their mouths... Honestly, if we old folks weren't hand-holding them every step of the way...

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: I've said it before, and I'll say it again: Liyue's ships are the face of the nation. We should be aiming for perfection every time! Each spot you miss with the paintbrush harms not just my reputation, but that of Liyue itself!

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Bah, I'm wasting my breath... You outlanders wouldn't understand anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Rex Lapis' death...

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Not now. I can't let myself be distracted while I'm at work.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: I'm getting old myself, and the thought did once cross my mind: Will the dockyard collapse into dysfunction after I die?

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: But the answer is no! The orderly functioning of the dockyard, and of Liyue, is based on centuries of tradition. Things like that do not simply disappear overnight... I, for one, will not allow it!

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: In the same way, if the Lord of Geo is truly deceased... Well, I will simply continue to do my job. Just as I have always done. To do otherwise would be to dishonor his legacy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Bah, hopefully not! Don't distract me anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Please, take a seat! The more the merrier!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hi.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Well hello there! Have you eaten? Please help yourself, we ordered more than we needed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You seem to be in a good mood.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: I certainly am! I'm out with my wonderful granddaughter — she's such a good kid. When I spend time with her I just forget all about the stress of the workday.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Also... To see the ships safely leaving the harbor and safely returning, it makes me feel like all my efforts are not in vain... Like it's all worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: See you! Don't scare off the stray cats and dogs on your way out — I'm about to go feed them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Rex Lapis' death...

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Hmph. There's nothing to be said. Someone did once ask me if Liyue would descend into chaos should Rex Lapis pass away...

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: My answer then was "no" — and now that the Rite of Parting has ended, Liyue Harbor's present state proves that I was right!

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Liyue Harbor has become a well-oiled machine over many years of development, one that will continue to run even in the absence of its creator!

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: That's all from me. There's still much to do! Manning our posts and doing our duty — that's how we will honor his memory!

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: I am Dockyard Manager Xiao. Is there anything I can help with regarding Xiao Lanterns?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want to trade Xiao Lantern materials.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: It's a pain in the neck when you're missing odd bits and pieces, isn't it? There's plenty of stock in the dockyard warehouse. Feel free to look around for anything you might find useful.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me more about Xiao Lantern making.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Xiao Lantern making is a traditional craft form at Lantern Rite. It's quite technical, you need to cut the paper, insert the wick, add wish sticks, paint it...

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: ...Overwhelmed? Don't give up just yet. Fortunately, only previous generations had to make them that way.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: These days, if you know how to use a Crafting Bench it makes things much easier.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Hopefully, the gods don't think that cheapens the wishes we make.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: The Crafting Bench is over there. Why not give it a try? Lantern Rite only comes once a year.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Manager Xiao
dialogues.text: Goodbye, and have fun!
